years.2026: BSc thesis in Maastricht, then the first months of the MSc in Utrecht.
years.2025: Second and third year of the BSc in Maastricht, and a research internship in the summer.
years.2024: Second year of the BSc in Maastricht.

projects.name: shortlist
projects.tagline: Sift, a job search app that scores postings against my CV
projects.text: Sift (the repository keeps its old name, shortlist) searches seven job sites, reads each posting and shows how well it fits my CV, with the reasons. It tracks applications, replies and interviews, and drafts motivation letters with Claude or a local Ollama model. Built for my own job search, with a lot of AI assistance.

shot.alt: Sift showing a job with its fit score and the reasons

projects.name: fairbatch
projects.text: Evaluation of FairBatch, a batch sampler that trains models towards demographic parity, on Adult, German and COMPAS over 10 seeds. It cut the parity gap on Adult from -0.19 to -0.03 and on COMPAS from -0.28 to 0.03, for 1.5 to 2.5 points of balanced accuracy. I also added a variant that updates the sampler from the measured gap.

projects.name: orthodontic-par
projects.tagline: PAR index suggestions from dental photos
projects.context: Rebuild of my 2025 internship work on public data
projects.text: Web app that suggests PAR index scores from intraoral photos for a clinician to review. The YOLO11s detector reaches mAP50 0.697 on the OMNI test set, above the dataset paper's best result (0.664).

projects.name: r-projects
projects.text: Two Quarto reports from the Utrecht machine learning course: predicting exam scores with cross-validated models and a tuned random forest, and clustering 5,000 IMDB reviews with K-means, a Gaussian mixture model and LDA. Group work, with each person's part listed.

projects.name: wichtel
projects.text: Secret Santa draw as a static site. Everyone gets a private link that shows only their own match.

projects.name: tagging
projects.tagline: personal data redaction in four languages
projects.text: Detects and redacts personal data in Luxembourgish, French, German and English text by combining a Rust rule engine with a GLiNER model. Recall on hard Luxembourgish names: 0.57 with rules alone, 0.91 combined. The rules also run in the browser.

projects.name: hyperreimpute
projects.text: Reproduction of HyperImpute on three UCI datasets, with a check against an older library version and tests of the method's limits. A CatBoost baseline with fixed settings beat it.

projects.name: record
projects.text: Windows app that records whatever your PC plays and saves each track as a tagged MP3 or FLAC file, cut at the silence between tracks.

projects.name: datapluck
projects.tagline: copy tables and charts as data
projects.text: Browser extension that copies any table or chart on a web page as CSV, LaTeX, pandas or R code. Private repository, in progress.

projects.name: pii-anonymisation-thesis
projects.text: Layout-aware anonymisation of student documents, tested with a re-identification attack. Recall 0.998 on 500 synthetic documents; the signals an attacker can use drop from 17.3 to 0.16 per document.

projects.name: fridgy
projects.tagline: scan a receipt, track the pantry, get recipes
projects.text: Mobile-first pantry app from a weekend team project. You photograph a grocery receipt, a vision model reads the items into your pantry, and a recipe chat suggests meals from what you already have. Missing ingredients go to a shopping list. Prototyped in Lovable; the repository is the cleaned-up code.

shot.alt: Fridgy sign-in screen on a phone

projects.name: job-recommender
projects.text: Matches candidates with job vacancies through a two-tower model, plus item-to-item retrieval for similar jobs. Group project; I built most of the engine. Private repository, code on request.

projects.name: recsys
projects.text: Group project on HotelRec, a large set of TripAdvisor hotel reviews. My teammates built matrix factorisation and a hybrid with sub-ratings; I built the content-based recommender, which describes each hotel by the TF-IDF of its reviews (stemming, bigrams) and falls back to popular hotels for new users.

projects.name: matlab-simulation
projects.tagline: random numbers, ECG cleaning and a queue simulation in MATLAB
projects.text: Individual assignment in plain MATLAB, without toolboxes: a permuted congruential random number generator checked with a poker test, outlier cleaning of ECG RR intervals with five views of before and after, and a discrete event simulation of a three-machine plant with maintenance.

projects.name: yolo-rcnn-pipeline
projects.text: Training pipeline from my orthodontics internship: YOLO and Faster R-CNN detectors for dental images. It was the starting point for orthodontic-par, which replaces it.

projects.name: team09
projects.text: Desktop app and research notebooks for a four-class brain tumour classifier (glioma, meningioma, pituitary, no tumour): duplicate removal, augmentation, a data dashboard, PyTorch CNN training with k-fold cross-validation and Grad-CAM inference in a PyQt5 interface, plus experiments on the BraTS 2023 data. Group project; I wrote most of the code.

projects.name: music-mystery
projects.text: Music guessing game built for an HCI user study, in a random and a personalised version. The personalised one keeps an Elo rating per mode and adapts hints and snippet length to the player.

projects.name: pizza-ordering-system
projects.tagline: pizza shop on MySQL, desktop and web
projects.text: Pizza shop on a 16-table MySQL schema with a customer and a staff app: orders, discount codes, a loyalty count, deliveries by postal area and earnings reports. Built as desktop apps for the Databases course in 2024. In 2026 I added a web interface on the same database and ordering logic, with a live order queue next to a street map; that web layer was written with AI assistance.

shot.alt: The web shop of the pizza ordering system

projects.name: tak
projects.tagline: board game AI with a hand-written neural network
projects.text: The board game Tak in Java with libGDX, playable against two AIs. One is minimax with alpha-beta pruning and a transposition table. The other uses the same search but scores positions with a neural network written from scratch, forward and backpropagation included, trained by self-play and against the heuristic agent. Group project; I wrote most of the code, including both AIs.
